title: Campaign: human motor cortex structure, what learned models add
abstract: Branch D of the human motor cortex structure campaign asks: Learned models: what do models trained across sessions and people learn that fixed analyses miss, and how does that scale? It splits by whether the claim is about what improves a model's decoding or about what its representation contains into leaves D1: What improves learned decoding most: more pretraining sessions or people, larger or different models, better recalibration, or more electrodes?; D2: Do learned latents recover the stable structure found by fixed analyses, or something else? No results yet. Cite this campaign and name the leaf to contribute.

citations.reason: Hahn et al. 2026, Nature Medicine: 20-year performance of Utah arrays in 14 BrainGate participants; the main source of summary data.
